skill.name: ai-agents-architect
skill.description: Guides the design of controllable autonomous AI agents, including tool use, memory, planning, evaluation, and multi-agent orchestration.
skill.summary: Design controllable AI agents with practical patterns for tools, memory, planning, and orchestration.
skill.author: sickn33

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 321 uses backticks only for Markdown inline code around related skill names. It does not execute shell commands or instruct the model to run external commands.
Lines 119-120 describe storing and resuming checkpoint state for agent recovery. There is no network scanning, host discovery, or reconnaissance instruction.

content.value_statement: Agent systems often fail through loops, vague tools, and weak recovery. This skill gives practical architecture patterns for controllable agents, memory, planning, tools, and multi-agent workflows.
actual_capabilities: Explains ReAct and plan-and-execute agent loop patterns.
Guides tool registry design with schemas, examples, and lazy loading.
Describes hierarchical memory with working, episodic, and semantic layers.
Identifies sharp edges such as unlimited loops, silent tool errors, and fragile parsing.
limitations: It provides architectural guidance, not runnable agent code.
It requires users to validate designs against their own runtime and tool permissions.
It does not choose one framework or hosted model for every project.
It does not replace security review for autonomous workflows.

use_cases.title: Design a tool-using assistant
use_cases.description: Choose an agent loop, define tool contracts, and plan error handling before implementation.

use_cases.title: Plan multi-agent coordination
use_cases.description: Decide whether supervisors and specialist agents are justified for a complex workflow.

use_cases.title: Review agent risks
use_cases.description: Assess loop limits, memory scope, observability, and recovery paths before release.

prompt_templates.title: Choose an agent pattern
prompt_templates.prompt: Use ai-agents-architect to recommend an agent pattern for [task]. Include loop type, tools, limits, and failure handling.

prompt_templates.title: Design tool contracts
prompt_templates.prompt: Use ai-agents-architect to define tools for [agent]. Include purpose, parameters, examples, error cases, and when not to use each tool.

prompt_templates.title: Plan memory and recovery
prompt_templates.prompt: Use ai-agents-architect to design memory and checkpoint recovery for [workflow]. Separate working, episodic, and semantic memory needs.

prompt_templates.title: Evaluate multi-agent design
prompt_templates.prompt: Use ai-agents-architect to critique this multi-agent design: [design]. Identify coordination risks, simpler alternatives, observability needs, and release safeguards.

output_examples.input: Design a research assistant that can search documents and summarize findings.
output: Use a ReAct loop with a small tool set for retrieval and summarization.
Set iteration, timeout, and token limits before deployment.
Keep long-term memory selective and cite retrieved sources in outputs.

output_examples.input: Review a proposed supervisor with three specialist agents.
output: Confirm that one agent cannot solve the workflow with better tools.
Define handoff contracts and failure paths for each specialist.
Trace delegated tasks, tool calls, latency, and final aggregation.

output_examples.input: Improve an agent that fails when tool outputs change format.
output: Replace brittle parsing with structured output or function calling.
Add retry instructions for malformed responses.
Return tool errors to the agent with recovery hints.

best_practices: Set iteration, timeout, token, and cost limits for every agent loop.
Write tool descriptions with purpose, parameters, examples, and known errors.
Log tool calls, decisions, latency, and token usage for debugging.
anti_patterns: Launching multi-agent systems before proving one focused agent is insufficient.
Catching tool exceptions silently and letting the agent continue with bad data.
Storing every observation in memory without filtering or summarizing.

faq.question: What does this skill help design?
faq.answer: It helps design autonomous AI agents with tool use, memory, planning, recovery, and orchestration patterns.

faq.question: Does it generate production code?
faq.answer: It focuses on architecture guidance. Users still need to implement and test code in their own environment.

faq.question: Which assistants can use it?
faq.answer: It supports Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as a text-based guidance skill.

faq.question: Can it help with multi-agent systems?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains supervisor patterns, specialist agents, delegation, aggregation, and coordination risks.

faq.question: Does it cover agent safety?
faq.answer: Yes. It emphasizes limits, clear failures, error visibility, logging, and controlled autonomy.

faq.question: When should I avoid using this skill?
faq.answer: Avoid it when the task is unrelated to agent architecture, tool use, planning, memory, or multi-agent design.
